grade.first_issue: The first decisive defect is the claim that if \(\mathcal P(a_{n+1})\) is an inclusion-minimal member of \(\mathcal G_n\cup\{\mathcal P(a_{n+1})\}\), then it is a minimal hitting set of \(\mathcal G_n\). This is false. For the admissible start \(a_1=15\), one has \(a_2=18\), \(\mathcal G_1=\{\{3,5\}\}\), and \(\mathcal P(a_2)=\{2,3\}\), which is minimal in \(\mathcal G_2\); nevertheless, for \(q=2\) there is no \(S_q\in\mathcal G_1\) with \(\mathcal P(a_2)\cap S_q=\{2\}\). Thus the asserted monotonicity and stabilization of \(P_n\) are not proved. This is an unsupported central structural inference under Rule E.
grade.summary: The hitting-set reformulation and the eventual bounded-gap argument are meaningful progress, and periodicity would follow conditionally from stabilization of a finite family. However, the central proof that the relevant prime set and family stabilize relies on false or unsupported assertions. Moreover, the submission concludes only \(a_{n+T}=a_n+L\) for sufficiently large \(n\), whereas the problem requires it for every positive \(n\); this independently invokes Rule D's ceiling of 3. Establishing the required global finiteness and pure, rather than eventual, translation periodicity needs a new central argument.
strengths: Correctly reformulates the gcd conditions in terms of hitting sets of prime supports.
Correctly observes that the minimum product of a minimal hitting set is nondecreasing and bounded, yielding an eventual uniform bound on consecutive gaps.
Once a fixed finite family \(\mathcal G\) is assumed, the residue-class argument correctly gives eventual translation periodicity.

errors.description: Inclusion-minimality among the supports already appearing does not imply minimality as a hitting set. Consequently, the deduction \(\mathcal P(a_{n+1})\subseteq P_n\), and hence that \(P_n\) is eventually non-increasing, is invalid.

The subsequent stabilization argument is also unsupported: the claimed growth of gaps between \(P\)-smooth numbers is nontrivial and unproved, and in any event \(a_n\) need not itself be \(P\)-smooth, so the bound \(a_{n+1}-a_n\le m\) does not exclude a \(P\)-smooth \(a_{n+1}\).
The final conclusion holds only for \(n\ge N\). No compatibility argument extends the same fixed \(T,L\) to the finite initial segment, so the required all-\(n\) quantifier is unhandled (Rule D).
